incidents.symptoms: 500 error rate on payments-api jumped from 0.2% to 34% at 09:20. HikariCP logs: 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms'. Postgres pg_stat_activity near max_connections (198/200).
incidents.root_cause: Connection pool exhaustion after a marketing email drove a 3x traffic spike; pool_size=50 per replica x 4 replicas exceeded Postgres max_connections.
incidents.resolution: Terminated idle-in-transaction sessions, then lowered pool_size to 40 and deployed PgBouncer in transaction-pooling mode.
incidents.what_worked: Killing idle-in-transaction backends dropped active connections instantly; PgBouncer prevented recurrence.

incidents.symptoms: checkout-service p99 latency spiked from 180ms to 4.2s at 14:03, right after Redis was restarted for a version upgrade. Cache hit rate fell to ~5%, Postgres CPU hit 95%.
incidents.root_cause: Cache stampede: all keys cold after Redis restart, and identical TTLs caused synchronized expiries; every request hit the DB.
incidents.resolution: Enabled single-flight rebuild on hot keys and added jittered TTLs (base +/- 20%). Warmed the top 200 catalog keys.
incidents.what_worked: Single-flight lock + jittered TTL eliminated the thundering herd; DB CPU recovered within 6 minutes.

incidents.symptoms: orders-api pods in CrashLoopBackOff. kubectl describe shows 'Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, exit code 137'. Started 8 minutes after release v3.4.0.
incidents.root_cause: Memory regression in v3.4.0: an unbounded in-memory cache of order objects leaked under load, breaching the 512Mi limit.
incidents.resolution: Rolled back to v3.3.9 with 'kubectl rollout undo', then shipped a fix bounding the cache with an LRU of 10k entries.
incidents.what_worked: Immediate rollback stopped the OOMKills; error rate returned to baseline within 3 minutes of rollback.

incidents.symptoms: payments-api returning 502s. Error rate 41%. Spike started exactly at 11:10, one minute after deploy of v5.2.0. Healthy old replicas still serving.
incidents.root_cause: Bad deploy: v5.2.0 introduced a null-pointer on the refund path when 'currency' was missing, crashing the request handler.
incidents.resolution: Rolled back to v5.1.4, froze the payments pipeline, and added a regression test for missing-currency refunds.
incidents.what_worked: Rollback first, diagnose second: 502s cleared within 2 minutes of reverting the deploy.

incidents.symptoms: Kafka consumer lag on 'notifications' topic climbing (now 1.2M messages). Consumer group rebalancing repeatedly. Logs show 'CommitFailedException: rebalance'.
incidents.root_cause: max.poll.interval.ms too low for a slow downstream email provider; consumers exceeded it, triggering constant rebalances.
incidents.resolution: Raised max.poll.interval.ms, reduced max.poll.records, and moved the slow email call behind an async queue.
incidents.what_worked: Lowering max.poll.records to 100 stopped the rebalance loop; lag drained over 40 minutes.

incidents.symptoms: checkout-service 503s at 16:53. HikariCP timeouts again; Postgres connections maxed. Coincided with a flash-sale traffic spike (4x baseline).
incidents.root_cause: Connection pool exhaustion under flash-sale load — same failure mode as INC-2041 but on checkout-service, which had not yet adopted PgBouncer.
incidents.resolution: Rolled out PgBouncer to checkout-service and right-sized the pool; added a load-shedding limiter at the edge.
incidents.what_worked: PgBouncer transaction pooling (the fix from INC-2041) resolved it; recovery in ~5 minutes.

incidents.symptoms: search-api latency p95 up 6x. Elasticsearch cluster status RED, one primary shard unassigned after a node ran out of disk (watermark flood-stage 95%).
incidents.root_cause: Disk saturation on a data node from unrotated index growth tripped the flood-stage watermark, making indices read-only.
incidents.resolution: Cleared old indices with ILM, added disk, and cleared the read-only-allow-delete block.
incidents.what_worked: Deleting stale indices freed disk below the watermark; shard reassigned and status returned to GREEN.

incidents.symptoms: orders-api 500s at 22:05, 90 seconds after deploy v4.1.0. Clean before/after edge on the error graph aligned to the release.
incidents.root_cause: Bad deploy: a DB migration in v4.1.0 renamed a column the old code path still referenced during the rolling update.
incidents.resolution: Rolled back app, made the migration backward-compatible (expand/contract), and re-deployed.
incidents.what_worked: Rollback cleared errors immediately; expand/contract migration pattern prevented recurrence.
